---
title: "04 · Monitoring outcomes"
subtitle: "Design observations around an outcome partners choose"
---

::: {.lead}
Monitoring becomes useful when the desired outcome, the observations and the decision are connected. This module supplies a protocol and working analysis code. No partner treatment observations have been supplied, so this prototype reports no treatment outcome estimates.
:::

## Start with an outcome

| Outcome to consider with partners | A possible observation | What it would not establish alone |
|---|---|---|
| A locally selected vegetation objective | Repeated field observations using an agreed indicator | Species identity, cultural value or use quality from a generic greenness index |
| Community protection | Changes in fuels and a documented exposure question | The number of disasters “prevented” by one treatment |
| Continuity of stewardship | Partner-defined records of work, access or training | Cultural continuity from acres burned |
| Smoke or watershed concerns | Appropriately located observations with meteorological or hydrologic context | Causation from a regional satellite signal alone |

These are prompts, not a prescribed set of indicators. Sensitive knowledge need not be turned into a dataset to have a place in the research.

## Specify the design before analysis

The protocol records the question, selected indicator and units, sampling units, treatment date, before/after windows, comparison selection, seasonality, quality rules and intended interpretation. Preserve a dated design before viewing outcome contrasts.

For the included paired workflow, each pair contains one treated unit and one distinct comparison unit, each observed before and after. Enter one predeclared aggregate per unit-period. Pixels or repeat visits within one unit are not independent treatment replicates.

## What the code calculates

For each pair:

$$
\text{paired contrast} = (T_{after}-T_{before}) - (C_{after}-C_{before})
$$

The code checks that the four observations exist, units and methods match, dates are ordered, quality flags are accepted, and a unit is not reused across independent pairs. It returns pair-level changes and a descriptive summary. A pair-bootstrap interval is produced only with at least ten independent pairs and remains conditional on the design assumptions.

## What the contrast means

A before/after comparison can be affected by drought, seasonality, treatment selection, different starting conditions and other disturbances. A single before period cannot establish parallel trends. The calculated contrast is descriptive unless the research design supports stronger identification. Remote-sensing greenness is not a direct measure of biodiversity, fuel safety or cultural benefit.

Partner records stay outside the website build. The research notebook can read a locally supplied CSV and writes no public results automatically. Sharing any resulting table, figure or notebook requires a separate release decision.

::: {.worksheet}
**Exercise:** write a protocol for a hypothetical vegetation indicator. In explicitly hypothetical arithmetic, a treated unit changes from 10 to 14 and a comparison unit from 8 to 9. Calculate the contrast, then explain two reasons it cannot by itself establish a treatment effect. These numbers are teaching values, not observations from any case.
:::
